narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Twelve hundred times one lakh makes twelve crore, and that is only one pair.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But twelve thousand times ten thousand also makes twelve crore.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is a second pair, so the slip is struck out.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble appears with only one pair; 12,000 × 10,000 = 12,00,00,000 is written; the slip is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Make a hundred from four twenty fives.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Move zeros between factors to find many pairs.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>There is no one right pair for the last part.
removed_beats.on_screen: the words four 25s make 100 appear; the words move the zeros appear; several pairs are listed

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip finds one pair for the last part and stops. Many pairs have the same product, because zeros can move from one factor to the other.
